Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
refactor(Wind): Remove mock sync sleep from MountainSyncHelper

Strip the `Effect.sleep(10)` used as a simulated sync delay and its "Mock sync for now" comment from the `SyncNowEffect` generator. The Mountain, IPC, and Telemetry services are already injected (though currently unused, denoted by underscore-prefixed parameters), and telemetry logging of the sync attempt is in place; the artificial sleep was the last piece of test scaffolding blocking a real sync cycle.

Introduce the `Documentation/GitHub/Architecture.md` file to describe the Wind UI service layer. This document details the Effect-TS native implementation that replaces VS Code's Electron IPC pipeline with typed Tauri commands routed to the Mountain Rust backend.

Key contents include:
- Overview of the `Preload.ts` shim and `Effect/` service modules.
- Explanation of the Define/Implement/Problem pattern for service construction.
- Description of Layer composition (`TauriLiveLayer`, `ElectronLiveLayer`, `TestLayer`).
- Mapping of Wind services to Mountain Tauri commands via `Effect/Mountain.ts`.
- Integration flows with the VS Code workbench and Sky UI component layer.

This documentation serves as the primary reference for the frontend service contracts and architectural boundaries between Wind, Mountain, and Sky.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Wind): Resolve macOS APFS path mismatch in configuration resolution

On macOS APFS, the workspace folder URI often carries a trailing slash while file URIs do not. This discrepancy causes `IUriIdentityService.extUri.relativePath` and `ILabelService.getUriLabel` to fail path computation, resulting in breadcrumbs rendering absolute paths (e.g., `/Volumes/<vol>/...`) instead of relative ones.

Update `ResolveConfiguration` to strip a single trailing slash from the resolved workspace folder URI. This ensures the workspace root aligns with the workbench's file URI normalization strategy, restoring correct relative path display in the breadcrumb and label services.

This aligns the configuration logic with the Tauri IPC substrate's path handling requirements established in the recent migration.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Wind): Strip trailing slash from workspace folder URI parameter

Mountain's `BuildInitialUrl` sources the initial workspace from `~/.land/workspaces/RecentlyOpened.json`, which stores URIs with a trailing slash. After stripping the `file://` scheme and percent-encoding the path for the `?folder=` query parameter, the decoded value still ends in `/`. On macOS APFS, a workspace folder URI with a trailing slash prevents `IUriIdentityService.extUri.relativePath` and `ILabelService.getUriLabel` from computing relative paths, causing breadcrumbs to render absolute `/Volumes/...` paths instead of workspace-relative segments like `Source > Foo > Bar`.

Normalize the decoded `folder` value by stripping trailing slashes (preserving a bare root `/`) before constructing the URI. Tighten the `Workspace` identifier guard to only build the object when a normalized folder parameter is present.

Message:
fix(Wind): Reduce IPC logging to prevent channel saturation during extension boot

The Tauri IPC channel was being saturated during extension boot by excessive _DevLogForward calls:
- Successful "tauri-invoke" completions logged every invoke (redundant - Mountain's Rust side already logs ok/fail with ns precision via `[DEV:IPC] done:`)
- All fire-and-forget channel stubs logged (noop/value cases are routine)

This caused keystroke lag as user input queued behind the log noise on the shared WebKit message channel. Fix removes:
- Success-case tauri-invoke forward (failures still forwarded - stack traces are worth the cost)
- Fire-and-forget channel stub logging entirely
- Only forward `drift` disposition case (the noteworthy scenario)

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:

Add a new regex-based codegen system that walks the VS Code source tree and extracts `createDecorator(...)` sites along with their interface members:

- `ExtractDecoratorMatch`: Captures decorator export names, tags, and JSDoc from `createDecorator<I<X>>('x')` patterns
- `ExtractInterfaceMembers`: Extracts typed interface members (properties, methods, events, getters, setters) with parameters and doc comments

- `SourceTreeWalker`: Async-iterator over VS Code TypeScript sources, skipping test/build/node_modules directories
- Typed records: `ServiceDecoratorRecord`, `InterfaceMemberRecord`, `CodegenProblem` ADT for error handling

Also adds `LandWorkbenchGlobal.ts` - a typed wrapper around `globalThis.__CEL_WIND__` that exposes `CELWind().RunPromise(...)` for Sky consumers without touching the raw global. Dispatches `cel:wind-ready` on installation.

This infrastructure enables automated Wind-side bridge shape generation from upstream VS Code source, with source-line back-links for traceability.

Message:
fix(Wind): Use username in dev PostHog identifier fallback

The previous implementation used `Date.now()` in the PostHog identifier fallback, generating a different random seed for every editor launch. This made it difficult to correlate telemetry events from the same development machine across sessions.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:

Add four new stub channel definitions to TauriMainProcessService's StubChannels to prevent "Unknown method" errors during workbench boot:

- `webview`: IWebviewManagerService stub - disables native menu shortcuts in electron but is no-op in Tauri's WKWebView
- `watcher`: IFileWatcherService stub - Land routes file watching via Mountain's FileWatcher.Register IPC instead
- `urlHandler`: IURLService stub - vscode:// URI handlers register through this; stub to no-ops for extensions calling registerUriHandler
- `download`: IDownloadService stub - extension gallery download path; returns undefined to surface "download not supported"

tag/message) so Tauri's param-case handling doesn't require a guess -
the Rust command coalesces whichever arrived populated. Add fallback to

boot, reducing startup latency.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Bridge VS Code dialog channels to Tauri's native dialog plugin

Add a native-host dialog bridge to IPCRendererShim that intercepts Electron-style dialog IPC channels (`nativeHost:showOpenDialog`, `vscode:showOpenDialog`, etc.) and translates them to Tauri's dialog API.

The implementation includes:
- `handleDialogChannel` async handler for showOpenDialog, showSaveDialog, and showMessageBox
- Translation functions converting Electron's `properties: ['openDirectory']` flags into Tauri's `{ directory: true }` format
- Normalization of channel prefixes (nativeHost:, vscode:, native:) to extract the method name
- Fallback responses matching VS Code's expected return types when Tauri dialog is unavailable

Also adds `TranslateOpenOptions` and `TranslateSaveOptions` to the NativeModulePolyfill to ensure consistent option translation in both the IPC layer and the dialog polyfill.

Without this, "File → Open Folder" silently fails because Tauri sees no `directory: true` flag and defaults to a file picker.

Also adds `Source/Utility/Tier.ts` providing Wind's mirror of Cocoon's tier feature-gating system using Vite's `import.meta.env.Tier<Capability>` substitution.

Author: Nikola Hristov

feat(Wind): Add Tauri 2.x invoke compatibility across all polyfills

Update Tauri invoke calls in all Wind polyfills and services to support both Tauri 1.x and 2.x APIs. The invoke pattern changed from `window.__TAURI__.invoke()` (Tauri 1.x) to `window.__TAURI__.core.invoke()` (Tauri 2.x).

- Update InvokeMountain() in TauriMainProcessService
- Add TelemetryLive layer to Bootstrap configuration

All polyfills now check for Tauri 2.x first (core.invoke), then fall back to 1.x patterns, ensuring backward compatibility with existing Tauri 1.x deployments while enabling Tauri 2.x upgrades.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Tauri-native IPC routing and complete workbench configuration

Implement two parallel IPC pathways to replace Electron's ipcMain:

1. **IPCRendererShim binary protocol loopback**: Re-implement VS Code's binary IPC serialization (SerializeIPC/DeserializeIPC) to handle vscode:message events with loopback responses. Provides stub handlers for channels (logger, storage, configuration, localFilesystem) to prevent workbench hangs.

2. **TauriMainProcessService**: New drop-in replacement for ElectronIPCMainProcessService that routes channel.call() directly through Tauri invoke to Mountain's WindServiceHandlers. Eliminates binary protocol overhead entirely - uses plain JSON over Tauri commands.

3. **ResolveConfiguration**: Extend with full INativeWindowConfiguration including profiles, colorScheme, accessibilitySupport, and other DesktopMain fields. Also fix appRoot to strip origin (workbench prepends vscode-file://), and set VSCODE_DEV: "true" for relative imports.

This enables the VS Code workbench to initialize in the Tauri webview with either protocol path.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Wind): Enable WKWebView compatibility with relative imports

Set VSCODE_DEV: "true" in both Install.ts userEnv and ProcessPolyfill default config. This tells the Electron workbench to use relative imports instead of vscode-file:// URLs, resolving the WKWebView (macOS) limitation where custom URL schemes cannot be used with import().

Also fix potential null reference in ProcessPolyfill by deferring hrtimeStart initialization. The previous code called process.hrtime() at module evaluation time, but Wind sets window.vscode.process after Install.ts runs, not globalThis.process. Initialize to [0, 0] and let the actual timer start lazily.

These changes enable the VS Code workbench to render properly in the Tauri webview on macOS.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add History, Label, Model, and TextModelResolver services

Implement four new Effect-TS service layers in Wind that connect to Mountain via Tauri IPC:

- **HistoryService**: Manages editor navigation stack for back/forward traversal. IPC: history:goBack, goForward, canGoBack, canGoForward, push, clear, getStack.

- **LabelService**: Resolves human-readable display labels for URIs, workspace roots, and filenames (used in explorer, tabs, breadcrumbs). IPC: label:getUri, getWorkspace, getBase.

- **ModelService**: Lightweight in-memory text model registry. Maintains open documents with content/version/languageId. IPC: model:open, close, get, getAll, updateContent.

- **TextModelResolverService**: Resolves URIs to text model references with reference-counting dispose pattern (VS Code IReference<ITextModel>). Delegates to ModelService with ref counting.

Each service includes interface, stub implementation, live IPC layer, mock layer, Effect Context tag, and problem types following Wind's established pattern.

Also refactor TauriIPC invoke to use unified "mountain_ipc_invoke" command with {method, params} structure, and update all layer composition files to use Layer.provideMerge() chaining.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Decorations, Keybinding, Lifecycle, and WorkingCopy services

Implement four new Effect-TS service layers in Wind that connect to Mountain via Tauri IPC:

- **DecorationsService**: Manages file/folder decorations (badges, tooltips, colors) shown in explorer tree. IPC: decorations:get, getMany, set, clear.
- **KeybindingService**: Manages dynamic keyboard shortcut registration and lookup. IPC: keybinding:add, remove, lookup, getAll.
- **LifecycleService**: Tracks editor startup/shutdown phases (Starting, Ready, Restored, Eventually). IPC: lifecycle:getPhase, whenPhase, requestShutdown.
- **WorkingCopyService**: Tracks dirty state of open editor resources (unsaved changes). IPC: workingCopy:isDirty, setDirty, getAllDirty, getDirtyCount.

Each service includes interface, stub implementation, live IPC layer, mock layer, Effect Context tag, and problem types following Wind's established pattern.

Also reformat ESBuild configuration files in Configuration/ESBuild/ for consistency with recent commits.

style(Wind): Use POSIX sh shebang for build scripts

Update the shebang line in both Source/Run.sh and Source/prepublishOnly.sh from `#!/usr/bin/env bash` to `#!/usr/bin/env sh` for improved portability across Unix-like systems.

Reformat all ESBuild configuration files in Configuration/ESBuild/ and compiled Target output files from minified single-line format to properly formatted, readable code with consistent spacing, indentation, and line wrapping.

Changes include:
- Expand minified import statements (e.g., `import*as e from"..."` → `import * as e from "..."`)
- Apply consistent named exports format
- Add proper line breaks and indentation

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Tier 3 service implementations

Add the remaining VS Code service implementations to Wind's Effect-TS service layer, completing the service coverage:

**New Services:**
- StorageService: Persistent key-value store backed by Mountain's StorageProvider
- NotificationService: Toast messages and progress indicators via UserInterfaceProvider
- ProgressService: Progress reporting with location options (notification/statusBar/window)
- QuickInputService: Quick pick and input box dialogs via blocking IPC pattern
- WorkspacesService: Multi-folder workspace management
- ThemesService: Color theme get/set/list operations
- SearchService: Text and file search via native glob/grep

**Changes:**
- Integrate all new services into TauriBaseLayer and TauriLiveLayer compositions
- Add IPC channel handlers for each new service (notification:*, progress:*, quickInput:*, search:*, storage:*, themes:*, workspaces:*)
- Include Problem types for each service with proper discriminated union error handling
- Add Stub and Mock implementations for testing

Also includes code formatting standardization across all Effect files (import ordering, line wrapping, consistent style) applied during the service implementation work.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Terminal and Output service implementations

Add complete TerminalService and OutputService implementations to Wind's Effect-TS service layer, completing the Terminal service from the previous commit and introducing the Output service:

- **TerminalService**: Add Live implementation backed by Mountain's TerminalProvider via Tauri IPC (terminal:create, terminal:sendText, terminal:dispose, terminal:show, terminal:hide). Also add Stub and Mock implementations for testing.

- **OutputService**: New service for output channel management. CreateChannel creates named channels, Append/AppendLine emit text, Clear resets panel, Show displays panel, Dispose cleans up. Backed by IPC (output:create, output:append, output:appendLine, output:clear, output:show).

- **TextFileService**: Update Live implementation to use actual Tauri IPC instead of stub, adding Read, Write, Save, SaveAll, IsDirty, and Revert operations.

Both services are now integrated into TauriBaseLayer and TauriLiveLayer composition under "Tier 2 service layers".

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add Terminal service interface

Introduce TerminalService interface for Wind's Effect-TS based service layer, mirroring the VS Code terminal service. The interface provides methods for terminal lifecycle management:

- CreateTerminal: Creates new terminal instances with configurable name, shell path, arguments, and working directory
- SendText: Sends input text to a specific terminal
- Dispose: Cleans up terminal resources by ID
- Show/Hide: Controls terminal panel visibility

Also add TerminalProblem discriminated union for typed error handling with three variants: TerminalNotAvailable, TerminalOperationFailed, and TerminalNotFound.

This follows the same pattern established for Commands, Editor, Extensions, Files, Language, and TextFile services added in recent commits.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Implement Live service layers for Commands, Editor, Extensions, Files, and Language

Add concrete Live implementations for the VS Code service interfaces introduced in the previous commit. Each service now has a functional implementation backed by Tauri IPC to communicate with Mountain (Rust backend):

- **CommandsService**: Local handler registry for UI-side commands with IPC delegation to Mountain's CommandRegistry for extension commands
- **EditorService**: Editor state via Ref subscriptions with Monaco command delegation for selections/decorations
- **ExtensionsService**: Extension discovery and activation via Mountain's ExtensionManagementService IPC
- **FilesService**: Full filesystem operations (read, write, stat, mkdir, delete, rename, copy, exists, watch) with URI → path normalization
- **LanguageService**: In-memory provider registration tracking with local disposal support

All implementations use Effect-TS patterns with proper error modeling via discriminated union Problem types. The services are now integrated into TauriBaseLayer and TauriLiveLayer composition.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind): Add VS Code service interfaces for Commands, Editor, Extensions, Files, Language, and TextFile

Introduce six new service abstractions to Wind's Effect-TS based service layer, each modeled after corresponding VS Code services:

- **CommandsService**: ICommandService for command registration/execution
- **EditorService**: ICodeEditorService for editor lifecycle and selection management
- **ExtensionsService**: IExtensionService for extension discovery and activation
- **FilesService**: IFileService for file system operations
- **LanguageService**: ILanguageService for language feature providers
- **TextFileService**: ITextFileService for text file read/write/save operations

Each service includes:
- Interface definition with Effect-returning methods
- Problem type for error modeling via discriminated unions
- Context tag for Effect-TS dependency injection
- Stub implementation for compile-time compatibility
- Live and Mock Layer configurations

These interfaces establish the foundational service boundaries for Wind's re-implementation of VS Code's workbench services.

Message:
feat(Wind): Implement atomic UI services and improve bootstrap

This commit introduces the foundational Effect-TS services for the editor workbench layout and refines the initialization sequence to ensure robust pre-load global availability.

New implementations include:
- `ActivityBar`, `Panel`, `Sidebar`, and `StatusBar` services: These provide atomic, reactive state management for the UI shell. They utilize `SubscriptionRef` to handle item CRUD operations, active state tracking, and priority sorting via Effect-TS streams.
- `NetworkRestrictions` service: A security-focused service that enforces network policies by default (blocking telemetry, marketplace, and update endpoints) while allowing internal `localhost` and `Mountain` communication.

Refactoring and Integration:
- Updated `Layers/Tauri.ts` to include the new UI services in the `TauriBaseLayer`, `TauriLiveLayer`, and `TauriDevLayer`, making them available to the application context.
- Modified `Install.ts` to attach `preloadGlobals` (containing IPC, process, and config) to `window` and signal readiness via `__WIND_PRELOAD_READY__`.
- Refactored `Sandbox.ts` initialization to switch from event-based to a polling-based strategy when awaiting pre-load globals, increasing reliability for the Effect bootstrap.
- Minor cleanup in `IPC.ts` and reorganization of `index.ts` exports.

This change completes the transition of the editor shell's layout logic into the declarative, composable Effect-TS architecture used by `Wind`.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
refactor(Wind): Refine Effect services and remove local dependency submodules

This commit refines the newly adopted Effect-TS architecture in the `Wind` service layer and shifts the dependency strategy for the core Effect libraries.

**Dependency Management:**
Removes `Module/effect` and `Module/effect-website` Git submodules and the `.gitmodules` configuration. This indicates a shift to managing these libraries via standard package management (npm/pnpm) rather than local source pinning, simplifying the repository structure and build process.

**Service Robustness:**
- **Health:** Refactored service checks to consistently use `Effect.succeed` or `Effect.fail`, ensuring predictable error channels. Simplified `checkAllServices` logic to directly invoke the checker instance.
- **IPC:** Added strict typing for `InvokeArgs` from Tauri. Improved error mapping with explicit `mapError` pipelines and fixed promise handling in `listen` to prevent hanging fibers.
- **Error Handling:** Added `override name` getters to custom errors in `IPC`, `Mountain`, and `Telemetry` services for better stack trace clarity.

**Type Safety & Hygiene:**
- Renamed `SyncResult` to `MountainSyncResult` in `MountainSync` to prevent naming collisions.
- Removed unused imports (e.g., `pipe` from `effect`) and stale exports (e.g., `ConfigurationWithSyncLive`) from the public barrel.
- Updated `Bootstrap` to use native method-chaining `.pipe()` over the functional utility import.

These changes stabilize the post-migration codebase, improve developer experience with better error reporting, and align dependency management with standard Node.js practices.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
refactor(Wind): Migrate to Effect-TS native architecture and remove legacy Bootstrap

This commit represents a major architectural refactoring of the `Wind` UI service layer, moving away from imperative TypeScript classes and legacy bootstrapping logic to a fully declarative, Effect-TS-based architecture.

Key changes include:

1.  **Legacy Deletion:** Removed the extensive `Source/Bootstrap` directory structure (Core, Stages, Integration) and `Source/Desktop` services (TauriConfigurationService, TauriFileService, etc.). These have been replaced by composable Effect services.

2.  **New Effect Services:** Introduced core services within `Source/Effect/` to handle application lifecycle:
    -   `Bootstrap`: Orchestrates startup stages (Environment, Preload, Configuration, Services, Initialization, HealthCheck) using Effect sequencing.
    -   `Environment`: Provides platform detection and environment info (formerly Stage 0).
    -   `Health`: Monitors service availability and system health (formerly Stage 6).
    -   `MountainSync`: Manages state synchronization between `Wind` and `Mountain` using reactive streams.
    -   `Clipboard`: Migrated from `Source/Application` to `Source/Effect` with full Effect-TS error handling.

3.  **Dependency Management:** Added `effect` and `effect-website` as submodules in `Module/`, aligning with the project's commitment to Effect-TS for all application logic.

4.  **Build System:** Updated ESBuild configurations (`Configuration/ESBuild/Target.js`, `Compile.js`, `Wind.js`) to minify output in production and correctly handle the new file structure.

This refactoring consolidates the logic previously scattered across multiple classes and stages into a unified, dependency-injected `Layer` architecture, significantly improving testability, composability, and type safety.

feat(Wind/Integration): Replace Tauri fs plugin with Mountain backend file operations

This commit completes Wind's transition from direct filesystem API usage to full backend abstraction by replacing the Tauri fs plugin with Mountain's unified IPC interface for all file operations. This aligns with Land's architectural principle of delegating all privileged operations to the native Mountain backend through structured communication channels.

Key changes include:
- Refactored FileService to use `mountain_ipc_invoke` commands (`file:read`, `file:write`, `file:stat`, etc.) instead of direct Tauri fs plugin imports
- Enhanced MountainIntegrationService with actual gRPC call implementation via `mountain_grpc_call` command, replacing simulation logic
- Added comprehensive test suites for file operations and Mountain integration, ensuring robust error handling and type safety
- Updated configuration sync to include client identification and sync metadata for better observability

These changes strengthen Wind's production readiness by establishing real communication with Mountain for filesystem operations, enabling centralized file management, enhanced security through backend delegation, and improved monitoring capabilities across the Land ecosystem.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Wind/Integration): Implement Mountain health monitoring service and refine IPC abstraction

This commit establishes Wind's comprehensive health monitoring system for real-time observation of Mountain backend services, advancing Land's commitment to robust, observable cross-platform architecture. The HealthService provides proactive health tracking, service discovery, and automatic recovery capabilities through structured event-driven communication over Tauri's IPC boundary.

Key additions include the new HealthService in the Bootstrap layer, which monitors Mountain services via dedicated Tauri commands (`mountain_get_services_status`, `mountain_restart_service`) and events (`mountain_service_status`, `mountain_health_alert`). The service implements configurable heartbeat monitoring, error threshold detection, and exponential backoff recovery attempts, reflecting Land's effects-based approach to side effect management.

Concurrently, TauriFileService was refactored to use abstracted `mountain_ipc_invoke` commands instead of direct Tauri filesystem APIs, strengthening the separation between Wind's service layer and Mountain's native implementation. Configuration service validation was enhanced with type-safe key/value checking, and import statements were optimized across integration points for better code organization.

These changes significantly improve Wind's production readiness by enabling real-time health visibility and reinforcing the declarative IPC boundary between the TypeScript frontend services and Rust backend.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
refactor(Wind/Integration): Enhance configuration service resiliency and remove API mocks

This commit significantly improves the robustness of Wind's configuration synchronization with the Mountain backend by implementing proper error handling and removing development mocks.

In TauriConfigurationService, added graceful fallback to default configuration when loading fails, ensuring the application remains usable even with configuration file corruption. Implemented exponential backoff retry logic with conflict resolution for configuration saves, reflecting Land's commitment to reliable state synchronization across the Tauri IPC boundary.

Removed mock implementations from MountainWindSync and replaced them with real Tauri API imports (@tauri-apps/api/core), marking a key milestone in the Wind service layer's transition from development to production readiness. These changes ensure Wind can now establish real bidirectional communication with the Mountain backend via Tauri commands and events.

The simplied import in TauriIPCServer demonstrates improved code organization as the Wind services mature toward the final Effect-TS based architecture.
